## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical operational deficiency. The effluent pump is running but drawing no hydraulic load, indicating either a dry-run condition, impeller failure, or discharge line disconnection. This requires immediate professional attention. All other measured components are in good condition, but the pump fault prevents normal system operation and poses a risk of motor damage from overheating.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches and represents 22.9 percent of the total tank fluid depth. This is within the normal operating range and does not indicate an immediate need for pumping.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Component | Measurement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effluent Pump Current Draw | 1.6 A / 7.2 A nameplate | CRITICAL - No Load |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Good |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | Good |

**CRITICAL FINDING:** The pump is drawing 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps, representing only 22.2 percent of full load amperage. The pump is running but no hydraulic load is detected. This indicates the pump is operating without fluid resistance -- a dry-run condition. Possible causes include:
- No fluid present in the pump intake or discharge line
- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line

A pump running without fluid cooling will overheat rapidly and sustain motor damage. The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound, so the fault lies in the pump itself or its discharge path.

## COMPONENT CONDITIONS
| Component | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good |
| Effluent Filter | Good |
| Effluent Filter Soiling | Light |
| Dispersal Field Surface | Dry |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet |

The effluent filter was cleaned and reseated during this visit and shows only light soiling. The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding. The tank liquid level is at the outlet, which is normal.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE:**
- **Pump No-Load Condition (CRITICAL):** The effluent pump is running without hydraulic load. Immediate professional attention is required. Do not continue operating the pump in this condition. Have a qualified technician inspect the pump intake, impeller, and discharge line to identify whether the pump has failed internally or the discharge line is blocked, severed, or disconnected. If the pump cannot be restored to normal operation, replacement will be necessary.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is repaired and normal operation is confirmed.
- The tank solids level is healthy. No pumping is needed at this time.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure and System Operation
Your effluent pump is the heart of your aerobic treatment system. It moves treated water from the tank to the dispersal field. When the pump runs without load -- as it is doing now -- it is spinning freely without moving fluid. This causes the motor to overheat because there is no fluid to cool it. The system cannot treat or disperse wastewater properly, and the pump motor will fail if operation continues.

Do not ignore this problem or wait to see if it resolves on its own. Contact a qualified septic technician immediately. The repair may be as simple as clearing a blocked discharge line, or it may require pump replacement. Either way, professional diagnosis is essential.

### Tank and Filter Health
Your tank solids are at a healthy level (about 23 percent of tank volume), and your effluent filter is clean. Once the pump is repaired, these components will continue to work well with routine maintenance.
